title: Euler's Formula Explorer
description: Interactive visualization demonstrating Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i·sin(θ) with synchronized unit circle rotation and sine/cosine wave traces.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mathematics
Signal Processing
Complex Analysis
Euler's Formula
learningObjectives: Explain how the rotating green vector on the unit circle represents e raised to the i theta, with its real-axis projection tracing cos(theta) and its imaginary-axis projection tracing sin(theta)
Predict the values of cos(theta) and sin(theta) at theta equal to 0, pi/2, pi, and 3pi/2 by setting the angle slider and reading both wave traces
Explain why the sine and cosine traces are identical curves offset by a quarter turn, given that they are projections of the same rotating vector onto perpendicular axes
Trace how advancing theta through a full 2pi rotation generates exactly one complete cycle of each wave
Evaluate Euler's identity by setting theta to pi and confirming that e to the i pi equals negative one
